title: Make bd load the ids it already lets you create
what_this_does: bd currently answers the question "which project does this issue id belong to" two different ways. When you create an issue it asks whether the id starts with the project's prefix. When it loads the file back it guesses instead, by inspecting the text after the last hyphen, and for names like ben-w31-p0a it guesses a project called ben-w31 that does not exist. The file is then refused whole, so 550 healthy issues fail to load because of 31. This change makes the loader ask the same question the creator asks, and applies that one rule to the two other places that guess: the check that tells a rename apart from a foreign duplicate, and bd rename-prefix, which today hands a brand-new hash id to an id bd itself created. The post-merge git hook also stops throwing away the error it just got, and bd is rebuilt and put in place.
why_bother: Fleet stopped syncing beads at w31 and nobody noticed for months, because the hook prints a generic warning and lets the merge go green. The same names sit in four more repos, 102 ids in farmplanner, duke, investing and teaching, and after this they load with nothing renamed.

flow.label: One membership rule in the importer
flow.detail: handlePrefixMismatch and upsertIssues ask ValidateIssueIDPrefix, the function create already uses. A database with no configured prefix keeps today's behaviour exactly.

flow.label: Same rule in the two repair paths
flow.detail: RenameImportedIssuePrefixes skips ids that already belong here, so --rename-on-import stops mangling local names; repairPrefixes in bd rename-prefix stops minting new hash ids for them.

flow.label: The hook prints its error
flow.detail: Both hook templates in cmd/bd/init.go, and fleet's copy on disk, print what bd actually said instead of discarding it. The merge still exits 0.

flow.label: Build and put in place
flow.detail: make build, back up ~/.local/libexec/bd-real, copy the new binary over it. The backup is the exact binary running today.

flow.label: Prove it
flow.detail: Five ship-gate checks, including a real import against copies of farmplanner, duke, investing and teaching, which never touches the originals.

flow.label: Decide
flow.detail: Approve or send back through the page rail.

approving.plain: bd will treat an id as belonging to this project when it starts with the project's prefix, which is exactly what bd already does when you create one.
approving.detail: internal/importer/importer.go:234 and ~616 call sqlite.ValidateIssueIDPrefix (internal/storage/sqlite/ids.go:68) instead of comparing a guessed prefix from utils.ExtractIssuePrefix (internal/utils/issue_id.go:21). The guess stays where nothing is stored to consult: the error labels, bd init, autoimport, and detectPrefixes.

approving.plain: Two repair commands stop damaging names that were fine.
approving.detail: internal/importer/utils.go RenameImportedIssuePrefixes is handed the whole issue slice at importer.go:278, so today it would rewrite bd-w31-p0a to bd-p0a and collide it with bd-w45-p0a. repairPrefixes at cmd/bd/rename_prefix.go:236 gives such ids a brand-new hash id. Both adopt the same membership rule.

approving.plain: A failed import after a merge will show you what went wrong.
approving.detail: cmd/bd/init.go:880 and :934 currently run bd import with >/dev/null 2>&1 and print two generic lines. They will capture the output and print it. Fleet's untracked copy at ~/projects/fleet/.git/hooks/post-merge gets the same edit, since the template only reaches repos whose hooks are written later.

approving.plain: The 267 ids in the other repos are left exactly as they are.
approving.detail: They need no rename once the rule is one rule. Gate 3 proves it by running a real import against copies of farmplanner, duke, investing and teaching.

approving.plain: You get one local commit on your fork, with the binary you run today kept for rollback.
approving.detail: No upstream pull request, as you decided. The two commits between the running binary (00d653c) and the fork tip touch a config file and a work log, no program code.

rejected.idea: Add a check when the id is created, refusing names like ben-w31-p0a up front
rejected.why: Create already validates, with the correct rule. A second gate would leave bd with two rules instead of one, refuse names that load perfectly well, and fix none of the 267 ids already on disk.

rejected.idea: Rename the 267 ids in the other five repos, as I did for fleet's 37
rejected.why: That treats the symptom. Once the loader stops guessing, those names are valid and need no migration.

rejected.idea: Send the fix upstream to steveyegge/beads first
rejected.why: You chose a local commit. Upstreaming would make the fix wait on someone else while five of your repos stay broken.

rejected.idea: Make the post-merge hook fail the merge on a bad import
rejected.why: Out of the locked scope, which is that the real error prints. A hook that breaks merges on a bead problem trades one failure for a worse one.

risks.risk: A project whose prefix extends another's, say beads and beads-vscode, would claim the other's ids.
risks.response: None of the 18 configured prefixes in ~/projects/*/.beads/beads.db is a hyphen-extension of another. Create already behaves this way, so import stops being stricter than create rather than becoming careless.

risks.risk: A database with no configured prefix loses renames it accepts today, because the new check is false for every id when the prefix is empty.
risks.response: The plan reads the prefix once and keeps the existing comparison when it is empty. This was review finding F2.

risks.risk: Swapping the binary under agents that are running bd right now.
risks.response: bd runs are short and single-shot, and the current binary is backed up to bd-real.bak-w4, so rollback is a copy with no rebuild.

risks.risk: Fleet's hook edit is untracked and a later bd init could overwrite it.
risks.response: The source template carries the same change, so a rewrite writes the fixed version.

model_assignments.why: Non-rote: a semantic change to a shared tool with a data-loss-adjacent blast radius

model_assignments.work: Importer, repair paths, hook template and tests
